summary: I am a software engineer and mentor looking for a role with new challenges, particularly in cloud services. I have 8 years of hands-on experience in software development and a BSc in Computer Science.

description: I work on enterprise software and cloud architecture at IBM, building systems used by clients around the world.
Day to day that means enterprise design thinking, cloud-native applications, and architecture work, mostly in Azure and .NET Core.
I am certified as an Enterprise Design Thinking Practitioner and in Azure Fundamentals.

I joined as a mid-level engineer and left as a senior developer and team lead. I started out helping rebuild the company's website and ended up running a team of front and back-end developers. The work was mostly Azure, Terraform, and ASP.NET, including an IdentityServer4 integration that measurably improved load times and customer conversion.

As a senior developer I led a team of five under Scrum, and spent a lot of time trying to keep it a place where people could work to their strengths. We rebuilt the multi-national customer facing applications in React and TypeScript, and moved the back end onto .NET Core REST APIs, Service Bus, and NoSQL data warehousing.
It was the role where I learned to lead rather than just build.

A consumer-facing firm of solicitors that ran its day-to-day operations on its own software. I replaced older system components with C# and MVC3, designed and maintained ASP.Net web apps and APIs on an MSSQL back-end, wrote SSRS reports and TSQL stored procedures, and expanded the legal case management systems.
I got the business onto Git and Jira, led its first research projects into Azure, and helped upgrade data warehouse security to the ISO-27001 standard.

For my undergraduate dissertation, 'Accelerometer Games for the iOS Platform', I built a physics-based game for iPhone and iPad. It taught me Swift and SpriteKit, and what it actually takes to get something through App Store submission.
The University kept the game as a teaching tool and showed it at open days as an example of a final project.

nonTechnicalSkills: Excellent communication skills with customer- and stakeholder-facing experience.
Strong experience with Agile & Scrum methodologies as a senior engineer of a product team.
Methodical, with close attention to detail.
hobbies: I shoot portrait and still-life photography, which is a good excuse to use both new and very old (and retro!) kit.
I pay a lot of attention to design, and it shows up in my work and my side projects.
